exposure: MR Pelvimetry measurements (anatomical conjugate, transverse diameter, anteroposterior diameter)
outcome: mode of birth (caesarean section due to CPD, assisted vaginal birth, spontaneous vaginal birth)
cohort: Primiparous women with a height of 160 cm or less were recruited from antenatal clinics.
finding: The feasibility study indicated that a full trial assessing MR pelvimetry's ability to predict cephalo-pelvic disproportion (CPD) in short stature women is feasible and acceptable, showing a trend of smaller pelvic measurements in women requiring obstetric intervention compared to those with spontaneous vaginal births.
mod_finding: Pelvic measurements, including anatomical conjugate, transverse diameter, and anteroposterior diameter, were observed to be larger in the spontaneous vaginal birth group compared to the in-labour caesarean section or assisted vaginal birth groups.
cross-section timing: MR scans were performed from 36 weeks gestation
